prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world each placement lands at the left-right mirror of the chosen anchor: a brick dx cells wide chosen at column x lands at column 8 - dx - x, in the same row. The valid-action mask is in the agent's own action terms. The designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The starting network collapses to DONE at once (0 placements, 100% DONE). The untrained trace shows why: the action-to-cell mapping is mirrored horizontally. '1x1 at col 2' fills col 5, '1x2 at col 6' fills cols 0–1, and '2x2 at col 2' fills cols 4–5, so the brick's real left column is X - dx - x. Rows are not mirrored. Every one of these steps fits that formula, while the reward fits the real filled cells, as expected. A translation-equivariant conv head therefore scores the wrong place for every brick. Placing usually costs reward, so DONE (reward 0) wins. The fix is to compute footprint scores in real cell coordinates, then reorder them into action indices with a flip that depends on footprint width. I also test a learned dense head that needs no knowledge of the mapping, which matters for worlds with other quirks. The baseline's 0.000 gives no noise estimate yet.

### Round 2
In this world the action columns are mirrored: action x fills column X-dx-x, and rows are unchanged. The target observation is accurate. A head that scores footprints at the real cells and then remaps them to actions takes dev success from 0.00 to 0.75. More updates (128 envs, 3 epochs, entropy 0.02) raise it to 0.91. That gap of 0.17 is much larger than the spread between seeds (about 0.04). The dense head that learns the mapping got stuck choosing DONE first (0.00), so a spatially aligned head is essential. In r1c2, training success was still rising at the end (0.85 to 0.88). Dev IoU is 0.99, and about 0.2 cells per episode land outside the target. So failures are rare irreversible misplacements, which more data or more context may fix. This round tests whether more samples and updates help (2 epochs vs 1 epoch at 64 envs). It also tests a deeper head with global context against the 2-epoch run, so the architecture change is isolated.

### Round 3
The mirror-aware head is what made learning possible here. Action column x fills real column X-dx-x, and remapping scores to match took dev success from 0 to 0.75. The current best, r1c2 (128 envs, 3 epochs, entropy 0.02), reaches 0.913 with both seeds working. The main way runs fail is the DONE trap: the policy learns to stop before placing anything. This happened with smaller update batches (64 envs: 1 of 2 seeds at 2 epochs, both seeds at 1 epoch) and with the dense learned head. The 64-env dilated network also failed on both seeds, so that result says little about the architecture itself. Recipes with 2048 to 4096 samples per update were reliable. Extra compute directly cuts training steps, and r1c1 shows steps matter a lot (123k steps gave 0.75, 162k gave 0.91). So this round keeps compute near 1x. The final pick is retrained on 4 seeds, so reliability matters. The candidates are: a higher learning rate, raw observations fed into the head, and a critic with its own trunk.

### Round 4
Placing logits at the cell each action actually fills (the mirrored head) is what made learning possible. It took dev success from 0 to 0.75–0.94. The best recipe so far uses 128 envs and 3 epochs. A 64-env recipe with 1 or 2 epochs made seeds fall into the trap of choosing DONE first: r2c2 lost both seeds, r2c1 lost one, and r2c3 lost both, so r2c3's architecture result is confounded with that recipe. Raising lr to 2e-3 helped a little: 0.9375 against 0.913, a difference inside the noise, but both seeds were good and the curve was still rising. Adding raw observations to the head did nothing. A separate critic hurt (0.52), so the shared critic seems helpful. The remaining failures are a few cells placed outside the target and stopping too early, which point to how the discount treats the end of the episode and to the lack of global context. This last round tests a higher discount, a higher learning rate, and a cheap global broadcast with the safe recipe.

## Trial it ended with
name: r1c2 with lr 2e-3
hypothesis: Same network and recipe as r1c2, but with learning rate 2e-3 instead of 1e-3. r1c2's training curve was still rising at the end (0.85 to 0.88). Because the rate decays linearly to 0, the last part of training makes small steps, and doubling the rate should finish the job at the same budget. Refuted if dev success is not above 0.913 by more than about 0.03, or if a seed falls into the DONE trap.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
